title: I have so many videos I could do about my time in Gander Newfoundland...
transcript: If you love Come From Away and you want to plan your own trip to Gander, Newfoundland save this video. I just got home from seeing the Come From Away production in Gander. It was one of the best show experiences of my life. One of the most incredible trips I have ever taken. And now I have so much advice, including how to book a screech in cause you gotta kiss the fish. To go to this production, to explore the incredible island of Newfoundland, to meet all the people and hear their stories firsthand, you have to do it. This is the fourth summer that Come From Away has run in Gander. This year it's running from June through September 13th. I believe there are shows Wednesday through Sunday, so make sure you're going when the show is running. There are not that many flights that fly in and out of Gander. You’ll most likely have to have a layover either in Toronto or in Montreal. I flew in Thursday night to Toronto and then Friday into Gander. Newfoundland also runs on its own time zone. It's on a 30. Like if it is 7:00am in Toronto or New York it is 8:30am in Gander. It's just important when you're realising timing and when you're booking things. There are two main options to visit Gander. One is to go through a tour company and the other is to plan it yourself. I think there are pros and cons to both. The nice thing about a tour company is you don't have to worry about hotels and transportation because both of those will book up early. There are not a ton of options on the island, and you will definitely need a car. Almost everything you want to experience will require driving. Of course, the thing I have to recommend the most is doing a screech in. Screech in is a fun Newfoundlanders ceremony where you get to do a couple of rituals and become honorary Newfoundlanders. You can do Screech In’s all over Newfoundland, but the Legion in Gander is especially meaningful because that's where the Come From Aways do it in the musical. And it's often lead by the reals, which are the real people who inspired the musical. Ours was lead by Brian Moser, one of the journalists who inspired Janice Moser Claude Elliott, who was the mayor in Gander during 9/11 and Beulah Cooper, who was volunteering at the Legion when the planes arrived. How is the sentence I get to say that's so wild? You can contact the Legion directly on how to book, either by phone or by email. They don’t hold Screech-Ins everyday, but they'll often have groups and they'll let you join. Some people have DMd me directly and have literally already done this. One person said they called and Beulah picked up and they scheduled with her. Gander also has these come from away interpretive panels all around the town. They Include first hand stories and photos. Find the map online of where they all are. Or you can go to town hall and pick up a physical map, but basically it lets you create your own Come From Away scavenger hunt. Don't only stay in Gander, visit the surrounding communities. Gambo, Appleton, Dover. This is from the Dover Fault where Nick and Diane fell in love. Nick mentions it's like a million stairs, but I did not find it that strenuous, wear good shoes obviously, but it's definitely worth doing. There are also guided visits available. We were with Oz Fudge, who was a police officer in Gander at the time and he's also in the musical. My biggest piece of advice though, is just talk to everyone. Everyone has a story and they are so unbelievably generous. And to see the show after you've done all of this makes the whole experience so much more meaningful. I have enough stories about meeting the “Reals” that I could do an entirely separate video, so let me know if you wanna see that. But go to Gander.
